Fixed in 4c9426ce4 (branch mine).

refreshThreadShellSummary no longer reads whole threads. Three of the four reads are narrowed at the SQL boundary: latestUserMessageAtByThreadId (MAX(created_at) WHERE role='user'), countPendingByThreadId (COUNT WHERE status='pending'), and listUserInputByThreadId (activity query + kind IN the three user-input kinds). The derive helpers are unchanged — only what feeds them changed.

Measured on the thread that caused this (40a5b1d3, 18,893 activity rows): 484ms to fetch and JSON-parse every row vs 24ms for the narrowed query. The live path decodes through Effect schemas rather than JSON.parse, which is why it measured 733ms of a 742ms command.

Two honest deviations from the acceptance text as written:
1. Not O(1). No index carries kind, so SQLite still visits the thread's rows to filter them. That is the residual 24ms. Left alone deliberately — t3code-1eg removes the row growth at source, so the scan stays small.
2. Proposed plans still use listByThreadId. Zero rows in production and bounded by turns-with-plans; the two-tier latest-for-turn fallback was not worth SQL risk for no measurable gain.

Rejected alternative: porting migration 024's SQL. Its pending_user_input_count uses a latest-state-per-requestId window function and checks 2 of the 4 stale-detail substrings, so it disagrees with the runtime fold. Adopting it would have silently changed behaviour. Tests now pin that divergence.

Investigation found explicit user-input waits, not lifecycle stalls. Disconnect, frozen-page, reconnect, and prompt-restoration tests passed; current UI clearly shows Awaiting Input.

Fixed in 86e68e7f7 + 44b29a169 (branch mine).

item.updated activities are keyed tool-updated:<threadId>:<itemId> instead of the per-delta eventId, so a tool call collapses to one row that updates in place. Streamed bursts are coalesced by a ~150ms leading-edge throttle whose correctness backbone is a trailing-edge timer that enqueues a synthetic flush onto the same DrainableWorker queue processRuntimeEvent runs on — so all cache mutation stays on one fiber and no terminal event is required.

The plan review changed the design in three ways, all correct:
1. threadId had to be part of the activity id. activity_id is a GLOBAL PRIMARY KEY (005_Projections.ts:49) while itemId is only unique within a provider session (ACP toolCallId / codex params.item.id are session-local counters). Keying by itemId alone would have moved one thread's tool row onto another thread.
2. Terminal-event flushing alone is unsound. turn.aborted was not handled in this file at all (emitted by CodexAdapter.ts:793, OpenCodeAdapter.ts:1534), and ACP leaves a cancelled tool call in_progress so item.completed never arrives. turn.aborted now has a branch; terminal events are an accelerator only.
3. A Cache is the wrong container for must-flush state — both TTL and LRU eviction discard silently. The trailing-edge fiber makes pending state live one window, so bounded storage stops being a correctness risk.

44b29a169 closes a race the implementation review found: the leading-edge branch dispatched without clearing a still-pending entry, so a late flush could re-dispatch the older activity and leave the row permanently stale.

Closed as superseded by t3code-zac, not as done. The problem is real; this approach is not the fix.

Why not done: NodeSqliteClient.ts:256-267 has one sqlite connection behind a semaphore(1) held for the whole transaction, and the projection fiber contends for the same permit. Moving projection off the command transaction improves ack latency but not throughput. It converts 'all commands slow' into 'all reads blocked' — the same silence the user sees. It would not have prevented the 2026-08-02 incident.

Why closed rather than left open: this bead is a trap for an autonomous loop. bd ready would surface it, and its own comments say do not resume as written. Better to close it and carry the question on t3code-zac, which has to land first anyway.

The attempt is preserved on branch t3code/74g-wip (b8a805302), pushed, DO NOT MERGE. Worth salvaging if this is ever revived: the awaitProjectedSequence barrier that dies loudly when called inside a SQL transaction, bounded 5s waits, loud halt on poison events that fails waiters instead of parking them forever, and a gapless bootstrap-to-live handover with an in-transaction cursor-skip guard.

Why it also failed on its own terms: gate red with flaky tests (3 failures on one run, clean on a rerun, all in diff scope), and two reviewers stayed BLOCK at the round cap — the snapshot-serving subscription paths (ws.ts:1389/:1413/:1511) got no barrier, which loses client events permanently, and the projection-lag metric had no test.

Reopen only if t3code-zac establishes that decoupling projection buys something once connection contention is addressed.
